Hypothesis: We hypothesize that in IDH-mutant iCCA, the accumulation of 2-HG selectively disrupts the local chromatin environment at fibroblast-activating cytokine gene promoters through inhibition of DNA/histone demethylases, leading to a focused increase in activating histone marks (H3K4me3 and H3K27ac) and a decrease in the repressive mark H3K27me3. This targeted epigenetic remodeling, validated through controlled temporal profiling and complementary assays (including ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq), specifically upregulates cytokines such as TGF-β and IL-6. The elevated expression and secretion of these cytokines then drive the recruitment and activation of cancer-associated fibroblasts, primarily those originating from hepatic stellate cells, which in turn remodel the extracellular matrix to establish a chemoresistant tumor microenvironment. Our investigation will employ advanced techniques including high-resolution spatial transcriptomics and CRISPR-mediated epigenome editing to dissect this cascade and to differentiate promoter-specific changes from global epigenetic alterations, thereby providing mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic intervention points.
Abstract: In IDH-mutant intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA), we propose that the accumulation of the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG) not only induces broad epigenetic alterations but also drives a highly selective, temporally regulated remodeling of fibroblast-activating cytokine gene promoters. Specifically, 2-HG inhibits key DNA/histone demethylases, leading to focal changes—characterized by increased activating histone marks (H3K4me3 and H3K27ac) and reduced repressive marks (H3K27me3)—at promoters of cytokine genes such as TGF-β and IL-6. This promoter-specific epigenetic reprogramming results in enhanced cytokine expression, which in turn recruits and activates predominantly hepatic stellate cell (HSC)–derived cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subpopulations. The activated CAFs orchestrate structured extracellular matrix remodeling that fosters a chemoresistant tumor microenvironment. Our approach leverages state-of-the-art techniques including locus-specific ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, single-cell RNA-seq coupled with spatial transcriptomics, and CRISPR-based epigenome editing combined with time-course analyses to not only elucidate the mechanistic cascade but also to differentiate selective promoter remodeling from broader epigenomic effects.
CausalChain: IDH mutation in iCCA -> 2-HG accumulation -> Inhibition of DNA/histone demethylases -> Selective epigenetic remodeling at fibroblast-activating cytokine gene promoters (with temporal dynamics and control over global vs. local changes) -> Overexpression of cytokines (e.g., TGF-β, IL-6) -> Recruitment/activation of predominantly HSC-derived CAF subpopulations -> Extracellular matrix remodeling -> Enhanced chemoresistance
